comparator.name: Law (Rechtsgeleerdheid)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 teaching and examination regulations specify 150 EC of compulsory study and 30 EC of electives. Students build from introductory Dutch law and legal skills to advanced substantive law, procedure and legal research. The 6 EC moot court and 6 EC thesis are separately required. Participation in the thesis assessment requires 120 EC including Legal Skills, and moot court requires 99 EC including Legal Skills. Professional and Personal Identity and Dutch language assessment are integrated requirements.

coreField.label: How law operates in a complex society and applying legal rules to current social problems
Critically evaluating laws and legal arguments; finding and interpreting legal sources

European Union law and fundamental rights

A 30-EC free elective/profiling minor chosen from seven Faculty of Law specialisations (or an approved external minor), preserved as open curriculum space

adjacentDirections.label: Legal challenges created by new technology

questionsApplications.label: Illustrative current-affairs legal questions the programme uses to introduce law to prospective students (moot-court pleading as prosecutor or defence lawyer, advising a start-up on legal issues, whether gossip channels can spread rumours unpunished, holding companies such as Tata Steel accountable, the legal limits of motorway demonstrations, football-violence enforcement, greenwashing, platform liability for identity fraud)

Further-study and career trajectories the programme prepares graduates for (master's specialisations in private law, international migration law, internet law, criminal law, and climate change/corporate law; the togaberoepen of lawyer, judge and prosecutor; government policy work; corporate legal advice)

audience.programmeDescription: Students develop legal reasoning through Dutch private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law alongside European and international law. They interpret sources, analyse cases, present arguments, take part in moot court and write a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination connects the study of private, criminal, constitutional, European and international law with the institutions that make and apply it. VU adds a sustained Dutch doctrinal sequence, civil and insolvency procedure, pleading practice and a legal thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The degree includes 150 EC of compulsory study and 30 EC of electives. Moot court and the thesis are separate 6 EC requirements.
